title: Seeing Inside LLM Inference: Observability and Cost Visibility for llm-d on Kubernetes
tldr: The llm-d observability and router SIG leads show end-to-end tracing of a request through the gateway, endpoint picker, KV cache lookup and prefill/decode pods, and use metric-to-trace-to-log correlation to find a bad scorer weight behind a TTFT regression. They then describe combining llm-d metrics with OpenCost to compute per-token, per-tenant cost, which is early work that is already upstream.

key_points.text: A request flows from Envoy to the endpoint picker (EPP), which checks KV cache state, picks prefill and decode pods, and a sidecar sends the prompt to prefill, after which decode pulls the KV cache GPU to GPU.
One trace covers tokenization, longest-prefix cache lookup, profile and scorer runs, endpoint selection, and prefill/decode; routing is a tiny part of the timeline.
Span attributes include the longest cached prefix in blocks, top endpoints and scores, TTFT and queue latency.
Grafana links metrics to traces in Jaeger with one click; logs carry trace and span IDs, but log-trace correlation is not in the dashboard yet, so you grep the trace ID.
Demo: a P99 TTFT alert led to a trace where the pod without the cache won because the cache scorer weight was zero, so the prompt was recomputed.
No error logs appeared; the EPP behaved correctly on a bad config, traced to a Helm release that changed the weight from 3 to 0.
Cost has two views: allocation (deployed capacity on given hardware) and usage (per-tenant, per-user tokens), with cost per token as total cost over tokens served.
llm-d router and gateway metrics plus vLLM or SGLang metrics go to Prometheus; OpenCost combines them with infrastructure cost and emits cost metrics at different granularities.
The goal is to compare self-hosted open-weights serving with sending requests to external providers, and to spot idle GPUs.
Dashboards, observability and the OpenCost integration are all upstream in llm-d.

numbers.text: Alert fired on P99 TTFT above 250 ms for more than 2 minutes; P99 jumped from about 200 ms to 600 ms.
Scores: cached pod 3.86 versus uncached pod 3.93 once the cache weight was zero.
Prefill took about 569 ms for about 4,000 tokens, 10x a healthy prefill.
Good vs bad trace for a ~3,800-token, fully cached prompt (59 blocks): 152 ms prefill with weight 3, 569 ms with weight 0.

open_gaps.text: Log-to-trace correlation is not supported from the dashboard yet; it relies on grepping trace IDs.
The OpenCost cost model for llm-d is initial work, still being evaluated in production.
Per-tenant and per-user cost granularity across shared models on mixed hardware is still being worked out.

opportunities.text: Use EPP trace attributes (prefix blocks, scores, chosen endpoint) to debug routing regressions.
Add alerts on scorer config changes, since a bad weight produced no error logs.
Add log-trace correlation to the upstream llm-d Grafana dashboards.
Feed llm-d and vLLM metrics into OpenCost to compare self-hosted cost per token with external API pricing.
